newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani textile exports seen rising in 1997/98.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani textile exports seen rising in 1997/98.

text.p: Pakistani textile exports, which rose 25 percent in the first 10 months of 1996/97, are likely to power ahead in 1997/98, a spokesman for the All Pakistan Textile Mills Association (APTMA) said on Monday.
Textile exports, which account for two-thirds of Pakistan's total export earnings, rose to 175.249 billion rupees ($4.522 billion) in July-April, the spokesman said.
"We expect a sharp rise due to incentives announced by the present government to boost exports," he said, without specifying the expected 1997/98 (July-June) increase.

An official of the state-run Export Promotion Bureau said total exports were likely to rise to $10.5 billion and imports to $12.5 billion in 1997/98, compared to forecast exports of $9 billion and imports of $12 billion in 1996/97.
